rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God needs no physical means and could carry whom He wills instantly; the means used in the Night Journey instead manifest the display of signs and divine honor.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ dilediğini bir anda herhangi bir mevzi‘e îsâl etmeye kādirdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says the Night Journey’s wisdom is to show divine signs, as the verse states, and the journey’s means serve to manifest honor.
rows.anchor: Fakat bütün bunlar irâe-i âyât ile izhâr-ı tekrim cümlesindendir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some exegetes cite the speed of celestial bodies and scientific examples to make the speed of the Night Journey and Ascension imaginable.
rows.anchor: Müfessirînden bazıları ecrâm-ı semâviye harekâtının sür‘atlerinden fennî misâller getirerek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı rejects natural explanations of a supernatural divine sign: an unprecedented event cannot be understood by analogy and is known only by observation or report.
rows.anchor: Hâlbuki misli görülmemiş bir hâdiseyi emsâl ile tasavvura kalkışmak tenakuz olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Burāq report offers a starting point for imagining the journey: its name derives from lightning, and its described stride suggests lightning or electric speed.
rows.anchor: Bu ise bir berk, yani şimşek ve elektrik sür‘atini anlatır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Burāq analogy can help imagine a rider traveling calmly without being shaken, but it only approximates faith to reason and cannot disclose the miracle’s true nature.
rows.anchor: Fakat bütün bunlar, nihâyet aklı nâkıstan kâmile takrib edecek iman delilleri olabilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ascension’s nature involves space, time, motion, and spirit, placing it far beyond the measure of human understanding and resistant to specification.
rows.anchor: Mi‘râc hârikası fikri, aklın mikyâs-ı idrâkinden çok yüksektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı evokes God inviting the beloved Prophet to visit and angels accompanying him, with Gabriel holding the mount’s stirrup and Michael its reins before God takes over.
rows.anchor: Nûrundan halk ettiği habîbini ziyaretine davet etmiş, melâikesinin havâssından gönderdiklerini göndermiş

rows.speaker: Molla Câmî
rows.claim: Molla Jami’s poem portrays the Prophet leaving his body like a garment at the Throne and proceeding beyond place, where neither body nor soul has ordinary spatial access.
rows.anchor: Molla Câmî kuddise sirruhu Mi‘râc’ın Arş’a kadar rûh me‘a’l-cesed cereyan ettiğini tasvîren demiştir ki

rows.speaker: Bazıları
rows.claim: Some hold that the soul has a subtle, non-elemental body and a dense elemental body; the Prophet left the latter behind, ascended in the former, then returned to it.
rows.anchor: Bazıları bununla alâkadar olarak demişlerdir ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says spiritual Ascension here does not mean a merely mental ascent; even if Sufi complete disincarnation occurs to saints, the Prophetic Ascension is a far greater divine sign.
rows.anchor: Ve elbette Mi‘râc-ı Nebevî’nin insilâhtan çok yüksek bir âyet-i ilâhiye olduğunda şüphe edilmemek lâzım gelir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited poem emphasizes that Muhammad alone entered the intimacy of Qāb Qawsayn; no other prophet shared that private audience.
rows.anchor: Muhammed’den diğer yok dâhil olmuş Kābe Kavseyn’e

rows.speaker: İbn Atıyye
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya and some exegetes read the purpose as displaying Muhammad himself to the cosmos as one of God’s signs, rather than only showing signs to him.
rows.anchor: İbn Atıyye gibi bazı müfessirîn لِنُرِيَهُۥ مِنْ ءَايَٰتِنَآ kavl-i kerîminin mânasını şöyle beyan etmişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı favors displaying the Prophet as a sign: the earlier-revealed Najm already says he saw the greatest signs, and Muhammad himself is among the greatest divine signs.
rows.anchor: Ve’n-Necmi Sûresi’nin nüzûlü daha mukaddem olduğuna göre hakkında لَقَدْ رَأَىٰ مِنْ ءَايَٰتِ رَبِّهِ ٱلْكُبْرَىٰٓ

rows.speaker: Cumhûr-ı müfessirîn
rows.claim: The majority refer “indeed He is the Hearing, the Seeing” to God: He knows the Prophet’s private and public words and deeds, recognized his fitness, and honored him with this station; the wording also threatens unbelievers.
rows.anchor: Cumhûr-ı müfessirîn, bu zamiri Allah

rows.speaker: Cumhûr-ı müfessirîn
rows.claim: On the majority reading, the verse shifts from third person to direct divine speech and back to third person, a rhetorical turn that also carries a threat to the disbelievers.
rows.anchor: Bu surette âyet gıyabdan tekellüme iltifat ile başlamış ve tekellümden gıyâba iltifat ile nihâyet bulmuş olur.

rows.speaker: Ebü’l- Bekā
rows.claim: Some exegetes cited by Abu al-Baqa return the pronoun to the Prophet, describing him as the servant who hears God’s speech and sees Him; Elmalılı finds no clear contextual cue for seeing God’s essence.
rows.anchor: Ebü’l- Bekā’nın naklettiği vechile bazı müfessirîn de zamirin Peygamber’e râci‘olduğunu söylemiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says that if the pronoun refers to the Prophet, seeing the signs shown to him is more apparent than seeing God’s essence.
rows.anchor: “O gösterdiğimiz âyetleri gören” demek daha zâhirdir.

rows.speaker: Tıybî
rows.claim: Tibi says the pronoun’s two possible referents hint that the Prophet saw the Lord of Glory and heard divine speech, in keeping with the cited hadith about God being his hearing and sight.
rows.anchor: Tıybî demiştir ki: “Zamirin böyle iki veche

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı contrasts Moses, who was met with “you shall not see Me” at the appointed meeting, with Muhammad’s journey toward vision, saying the difference between the stations of the intimate speaker and the beloved is clear.
rows.anchor: makām-ı Kelîm ile makām-ı Habîb beynindeki fark vâzıhan anlaşılır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah’s foundational guidance to Israel was to take no trustee or lord besides God and entrust their affairs to no other.
rows.anchor: benden başka vekil ittihaz etmeyin umûrunuzu tefviz edecek Benden başka rab tanımayın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Descendants of those carried with Noah” addresses humanity as descendants of the few believers rescued aboard the Ark; reflecting on this origin shows that no other patron should be taken.
rows.anchor: ey Nûh’un maiyyetinde gemiye bindirip tûfandan kurtardığımız birkaç mü’minin zürriyeti, yani ey bugünkü insanlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah was grateful in every state, and the address rebukes his descendants for ingratitude.
rows.anchor: O Nûh hakikaten bir abd-i şekûr idi her hâlinde şükrederdi yani siz neye nankörlük ediyorsunuz?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God decreed in scripture that Israel would corrupt the Holy Land twice and rise arrogantly; Elmalılı identifies arrogance as the source of their corruption.
rows.anchor: lâbüd siz, bu Arz’da (Arz-ı Mukaddes’te) iki kere fesat yapacaksınız ve lâbüd kabaracak kibirleneceksiniz fesadın menşe’i bu olacak.

rows.speaker: İbn İshak
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq dates the first promised punishment to Israel’s killing of the prophet Isaiah.
rows.anchor: İbn İshak’ın rivayetine göre Şa‘yâ aleyhiselâm’ı katlettikleri zamandır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı introduces Ibn Jarir’s detailed account as a useful moral narrative about Israel’s first corruption and punishment.
rows.anchor: İbn Cerîr Tefsirinde tafsil olunmuş olan bu kıssa, ibret alınacak mevâ‘izi muhtevî olduğundan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the account, earlier sins were met with divine forbearance; under Queen Sıdıka, Isaiah was sent and the Babylonian king Sennacherib’s invasion was repelled.
rows.anchor: Nihâyet mülûk-i Benî İsrâil’den Sıdıka nâmındaki melikleri zamanında vukū‘âtları büyümüştü.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Isaiah son of Amoz foretold Jesus and Muhammad; Queen Sıdıka followed his revelation and counsel, but after her death factional rivalry and killings spread and Israel stopped listening to Isaiah.
rows.anchor: Şa‘yâ b. Emsıya aleyhisselâm Îsâ ve Muhammed aleyhimesselâm’ı tebşir eden bir peygamber idi.

rows.speaker: شَعْيا
rows.claim: Isaiah’s oracle recalls that God had chosen, favored, healed, gathered, and protected Israel, but they then rebelled and killed each other without recognizing the source of their ruin.
rows.anchor: Halbuki onlar zâyi‘olmuş, çobanı yok davar gibi idiler. Öyle iken ürkenlerini yatıştırdı, yitenlerini topladı

rows.speaker: شَعْيا
rows.claim: Isaiah compares Israel’s ingratitude unfavorably with animals that remember their pasture, though Israel has reason and should know where its destruction comes from.
rows.anchor: Deve bile vatanını hatırlar da ona döner gelir. Eşek bile üzerinde doyduğu bağı hatırlar

rows.speaker: شَعْيا
rows.claim: Isaiah’s parable depicts people destroying a carefully restored estate; its wall signifies God’s covenant, palace the law, river the Book, guard the prophet, trees Israel, and bad fruit their wicked deeds.
rows.anchor: O duvar Benim zimmetim, kasr şeriatım, nehir kitabım, muhafız peygamberim, dikilen ağaçlar da onlar

rows.speaker: شَعْيا
rows.claim: Sacrificing cattle does not bring people near God, who does not eat meat; true devotion is piety and refraining from killing lives God forbade.
rows.anchor: Bana sığır, koyun kesmekle tekarrub etmek istiyorlar.

rows.speaker: شَعْيا
rows.claim: Building and ornamenting sanctuaries while hands are stained with blood and hearts remain polluted is hypocrisy; God needs no buildings, which were ordered as places for remembrance, praise, and prayer.
rows.anchor: Benim teşyîd-i büyûta ne ihtiyâcım var? Ben onlara sâkin olmam, Benim nakışlı mâbedlere ihtiyâcım mı var?

rows.speaker: شَعْيا
rows.claim: When Israel claims God cannot unite them or reach their hearts, the oracle says He can make two dry trees into one, and could likewise gather their community and command their hearts.
rows.anchor: Allah buyurdu ki: Söyle onlara, gördünüz ya Ben iki kuru ağacı telif etmeye kādirim.

rows.speaker: شَعْيا
rows.claim: Israel complains that fasting, prayer, charity, and tearful supplications have not been accepted, but the oracle asks what could obstruct God’s response and points to His limitless mercy and generosity.
rows.anchor: Diyorlar ki: ‘Oruç tuttuk sıyâmımız ref‘olunmadı, namaz kıldık namazımız nurlanmadı

rows.speaker: شَعْيا
rows.claim: The people could have seen that their own rejection of the wisdom God illuminated in their hearts and their preference for the world made them their greatest enemy.
rows.anchor: dünyayı iştirâ ettikleri hikmet ile nefislerine bir atf-ı nazar etselerdi, nereden vurulduklarını görürler

rows.speaker: شَعْيا
rows.claim: The oracle rejects fasting based on lies and unlawful food, prayer while attending to violators of sacred limits, charity from stolen property, and supplication contradicted by one’s deeds.
rows.anchor: Ben onların yalan sözle telbis ettikleri, haram yemekle kuvvet almak istedikleri oruçlarını nasıl kabul ederim?

rows.speaker: شَعْيا
rows.claim: God accepts the humble and hears the poor; mercy to the poor, support for the weak, justice for the oppressed, help for the dispossessed, and giving each rights-holder their due mark divine approval.
rows.anchor: Fukarâya merhamet, zu‘afâyı takrib, mazlûma insaf, mağsûba yardım

rows.speaker: شَعْيا
rows.claim: The oracle says that if speaking to humans were fitting for God, He would become their sight, hearing, understanding, and bodily strength and would steady their tongues and minds.
rows.anchor: Bana beşerle konuşmak yaraşsa idi onlarla konuşurdum.

rows.speaker: شَعْيا
rows.claim: Those who call the divine messages fabricated inherited talk from sorcerers and soothsayers hide their claims, although God knows the unseen and everything they reveal or conceal.
rows.anchor: Sen Benim risaletlerimi tebliğ ederek kelâmımı işittikleri zaman ‘bunlar uydurma laflar

rows.speaker: شَعْيا
rows.claim: God has decreed since creating the heavens and earth a judgment with an appointed term that will inevitably occur; the opponents cannot predict its timing or match God’s power and wisdom.
rows.anchor: Ben semâvât ve Arz’ı halk ettiğim gün kendime isbat eylediğim bir hüküm hükmettim

rows.speaker: شَعْيا
rows.claim: The oracle promises that God will raise this religion above all despite polytheists and reverse worldly hierarchies by giving prophecy, honor, strength, wealth, cities, and rule to the lowly and weak.
rows.anchor: Ben onu müşriklerin istememesine rağmen her dinin üstüne çıkaracağım.

rows.speaker: شَعْيا
rows.claim: Isaiah foretells an unlettered prophet named Ahmed, neither harsh nor rude, endowed with tranquility, piety, wisdom, truthfulness, forgiveness, justice, law, guidance, and Islam.
rows.anchor: Ben bunun için bir nebiyy-i ümmî ba‘s edeceğim. Sert değil, kaba değil, sokaklarda bağırmaz

rows.speaker: شَعْيا
rows.claim: Through the prophet, God will guide, teach, elevate, enrich, and gather divided hearts, desires, and peoples, making his community the best nation brought forth for humanity.
rows.anchor: muhtelif kalbleri, dağınık arzuları, müteferrik ümmetleri onunla telif edeceğim.

rows.speaker: شَعْيا
rows.claim: The prophet’s followers will worship God alone, enjoin right and forbid wrong, pray and fight in His cause, migrate for His pleasure, and remember and glorify Him in daily life.
rows.anchor: Beni tevhid için Bana iman ve ihlas ile mârufu emir, münkeri nehy edecekler

rows.speaker: شَعْيا
rows.claim: The oracle describes their purification and discipline, their sacrificial lives and scripture-filled hearts, as monks by night and lions by day, all as divine favor.
rows.anchor: kurbanları kanları, kitapları sîneleri, gece ruhban, gündüz arslan.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Isaiah finished, Israelites attacked him; he hid in a tree, was discovered by the edge of his garment, and was sawn apart with the tree, after which God sent Nebuchadnezzar against them.
rows.anchor: Şa‘yâ aleyhisselâm sözünü bitirince öldürmek için üzerine saldırmışlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite phrase “servants for Us” signals terror, not the special honor conveyed by an attached “His servant”; all creatures, believers and unbelievers, belong to God, making disbeliever domination over sinful believers frightening.
rows.anchor: Yani bu tenkirde عَبْدِه۪ târifi gibi izâfet-i mahsûsa ile bir teşrif mânası değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Communities that cannot be reformed through righteous leadership face this same fate.
rows.anchor: Sâlih ellerle ıslah kabul etmeyen akvâmı bekleyen

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some exegetes identify the attackers with Goliath, but most identify them with Nebuchadnezzar; Elmalılı says the essential point is the event’s nature and wisdom, not its people or date.
rows.anchor: Bazı müfessirîn bu vak‘anın Câlût vak‘ası olduğunu söylemişlerse de ekseriyet Buhtunassar vak‘ası demişlerdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı prefers considering the event according to the Qur’an’s account and purpose without trying to identify its people and dates.
rows.anchor: Onun için en doğrusu eşhâs ve ezmânın tâyiniyle uğraşmayarak vak‘ayı Kur’ân’ın beyânı vechile

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The attackers searched among the houses and massacred Israelites, searching even within homes for people to kill.
rows.anchor: umûmî mahallerden mâ‘adâ evlerin aralarını taharrî edip öldürecek Benî İsrâil aradılar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised decree for the first corruption was thus put into effect and completed.
rows.anchor: birinci fesad devresinde mev‘ud olan hükm ü kazâ bu suretle fiile çıkarıldı, tamam oldu.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı links the desolated aftermath to the ruined town in Baqara 2:259.
rows.anchor: Sûre-i Bakara’da أَوْ كَٱلَّذِى مَرَّ عَلَىٰ قَرْيَةٍۢ وَهِىَ خَاوِيَةٌ عَلَىٰ عُرُوشِهَا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God later restored Israel’s ascendancy over its attackers, supplied wealth and sons, and made its forces more numerous.
rows.anchor: Sonra da sizin onlar üzerine tekrar savletinizi iade ettik devletinizi tekrar verdik

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good conduct benefits its practitioners as obedience opens blessings; wrongdoing likewise harms them, as disobedience and corruption open worldly and afterlife punishments.
rows.anchor: eğer güzel işlerseniz Allah’a itaat, emr ü nehyine riayetle güzel çalışır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israel’s restored power was divine assistance and also connected with their good effort: discipline led them to repent and reform, succeeding after a hundred years.
rows.anchor: bir imdâd-ı ilâhî olmakla beraber aynı zamanda kendilerinin hüsn-i mesâîleriyle de alâkadar idi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The favor would not last: a second corruption would begin, followed by the final promised punishment and collapse of their power.
rows.anchor: Fakat bu ihsan devam etmeyip ikinci fesadları başlayacak ve o vakit son vaadleri gelecek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The later promise comes when Israel kills John and attempts to kill and crucify Jesus.
rows.anchor: sonuncusunun vadesi geldiği vakit ki Yahyâ aleyhisselâm’ı katl

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The attackers will humiliate Israel, enter the sanctuary as on the first occasion, and utterly destroy what they overran.
rows.anchor: yüzlerinizi kötületsinler için, evvelki defa girdikleri gibi yine Mescid’e girsinler için

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some reports name the Babylonian ruler as Cuder or Curdus; Elmalılı allows that the three terrible outcomes may be phases of one event or a sequence of distinct events.
rows.anchor: Mülûk tavâifinden Bâbil meliki Cuder veya Cürdus diye rivayet edenler olmuşsa da

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated purpose particle in the verse makes a sequence of multiple events more likely, in Elmalılı’s view.
rows.anchor: Her birinde “lâm”ın tasrihi ikinci ihtimali daha ziyade andırır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Historical information identifies the force that carried out this destruction as the Romans, from Titus through Constantine.
rows.anchor: bu tahribi yapan be’s-i şedîd sahipleri de ma‘lûmât-ı tarihiyeye nazaran Titus’tan Konstantin’e kadar Romalılar olmuştu.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı links the mosque’s destruction to Baqara 2:114, about blocking God’s mosques and striving to ruin them.
rows.anchor: Sûre-i Bakara’da أَظْلَمُ مِمَّن مَّنَعَ مَسَٰجِدَ ٱللَّهِ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised mercy is near through the sending of the latter-day Prophet, mercy to all worlds, and Israel’s hope of release from domination if it reforms.
rows.anchor: rahmeten li‘l-âlemîn olan Âhir Zaman Peygamberi’nin gönderilmesi ve sizin o tasallutlardan kurtulmanız ümidi artık yakındır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Israel returns to corruption, God will return to punishment.
rows.anchor: şayet yine dönerseniz eskisi gibi fesâda avdet ederseniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı glosses hell as a prison from which escape is impossible and says Israel’s decreed history had been disclosed in the Torah and later scriptures.
rows.anchor: cehennemi kâfirler için bir hasîr -çıkılması nâkābil bir mahbes- kılmışızdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an guides to the straightest and firmest path, announces a great reward to believers who perform the good deeds it describes, and warns of painful punishment prepared for those who deny the afterlife.
rows.anchor: Haberiniz olsun ki bu Kur’an, insanları en doğru yola hidâyet eder ve sâlih sâlih ameller yapan mü’minlere tebşir eyler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should respond with faith and good deeds, seek the great reward, and protect themselves from painful punishment.
rows.anchor: buna karşı insanların yapacağı şey, iman ile sâlih amelleri işleyip o büyük ecri istemek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans call for evil as if praying for good: they may ask for punishment as though it were reward, or invite it through their actions.
rows.anchor: insan, hayra dua eder gibi şerre dua veya şerri davet eder.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Impatience makes people demand the future before its time; instead of patiently seeking reward through faith and good works, they wish painful punishment on unbelievers to arrive immediately.
rows.anchor: İnsan acûldür pek acelecidir. Sonra olacak şeyi vaktinden evvel oluversin ister.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because premature demands can end in deprivation, believers should avoid praying for evil, patiently ask for good, and actively pursue it through righteous deeds.
rows.anchor: mü’minler şerre dua etmemeli, sabr u teennî ile hayra dua etmeli

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human haste also means preferring immediate worldly gain to deferred afterlife reward; Elmalılı says the next passage on seeking the immediate life clarifies this, while qualifying the trait as characteristic of the species or some states, not every person or circumstance.
rows.anchor: İnsan peşincidir. Veresiyeden ziyade peşine heves eder, âhireti dünyada görmek ister.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night and day are signs whose alternation measures time and points to the divine power that governs it.
rows.anchor: ihtilâf ve te‘âkubuyla zamanın cereyânına mikyas ve onun üzerinde icrâ-yı hüküm ve tasarruf eden kudret-i ilâhiyeden birer nişânedirler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı reads the concise wording as rhetorical interweaving: both night and day were made signs, each with its own sign, and the night sign was then effaced.
rows.anchor: bu nazım san‘at-ı ihtibâk kabîlinden bir îcâz ile şu mânayı iş‘âr eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night sign may mean darkness or the moon, and the day sign light or the sun; reading it as darkness makes its effacement redundant, so Elmalılı prefers the moon, with darkness implied.
rows.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh “âyetü’l-leyl”den murad Kamer olmak ve zulmet bunun mahvından anlaşılmak daha zâhirdir.

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the moon, the night sign, once shone like the sun, was effaced, and its dark marks remain as traces of the effacement.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas demiştir ki âyetü’l-leyl olan Kamer, Şems gibi mudî idi, mahvedildi

rows.speaker: Muhammed b. Ka‘b-i Kurazî
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka‘b al-Qurazi says night and day once each had a sun, and the night sun was effaced, leaving the mark now seen on the moon.
rows.anchor: Muhammed b. Ka‘b-i Kurazî demiştir ki: “Gece bir güneş

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: A report from Abdullah ibn Salam says he asked about the moon’s dark mark; the Prophet answered that both had been suns and that the mark was the effacement mentioned in the verse.
rows.anchor: Abdullah b. Selâm, Nebiyy-i Ekrem sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem’den Kamer’deki karaltıyı sual etti.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı concludes that the moon began as a luminous, hot sun, which God extinguished; its dark mark, changing phases, disappearance at conjunction, and reappearance as a crescent are effects of that effacement.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ o güneşi mahvetti yani söndürdü ve bu suretle şimdi bildiğimiz gece âyeti olan Kamer husûle geldi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although astronomers long knew moonlight was reflected from the sun, they did not know the moon had once shone like the sun and was extinguished; Elmalılı says modern scientists accepted this Qur’anic disclosure and built cosmological theories on it.
rows.anchor: Kur’ân’ın haber vermiş olduğu bu hakikati nihâyet zamanımız ashâb-ı fenni almış kabul etmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon’s effacement offers an early example for imagining the sun’s folding and stars’ dimming at the Resurrection; the passage makes time’s transformations a lesson about resurrection and the afterlife.
rows.anchor: âyetleriyle haber verilen tekvîr-i Şems, inkidâr-ı nücûm hâdiselerinin tasavvur ve tasdîkini

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun makes the day a means of sight; the universal address suggests humans appeared after the moon’s effacement, and the alternation of night and day supports human life.
rows.anchor: Arz üzerinde insan cinsi Kamer’in mahvından sonra vücûda gelmiş ve gece ile gündüzün tefrîki hayât-ı beşerin esbâb-ı feyzinden birisi olmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These signs let people live, see, recognize their Lord’s greatness, and work for good gain and progress from His generosity, rather than seek evil or deficiency.
rows.anchor: O’nun lutf u kereminden hayırlı kâr ve terakki istemek için çalışasınız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night, day, months, and years allow people to measure time and account for worldly and afterlife consequences, so they do not demand the future prematurely or forget the afterlife.
rows.anchor: zamanı ölçüp önünü sonunu dünyayı ve âhireti hesap edesiniz de sonra olacak şeyleri acele ile önden istemeyesiniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God distinguishes everything in creation and explains religious and worldly good and evil in the Qur’an; Elmalılı compares the Qur’an to the visible day sign and abrogated earlier scriptures to the effaced night sign.
rows.anchor: Bunun karşısında kütüb-i sâlife ise mahvedilmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every person’s bird tied to the neck signifies one’s fate or share of good and evil from the unseen, assigned to one’s own responsibility and choices, or the burden of one’s own sins.
rows.anchor: baht u kaderini, âlem-i gaybdan uçup gelecek olan hayır veya şer nasibini kendi zimmetine ilzam eyledik

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At resurrection each person receives an opened record of deeds and account and is told to read it; the self is sufficient as its own accountant.
rows.anchor: bir kitap -a‘mâlini kayd ve hesâbını irâe eden bir defter- çıkaracağız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı exhorts people to examine themselves daily and take their own account before they are called to account.
rows.anchor: insan dünyada da her gün kendini okumalı, hesâba çekilmezden evvel kendini muhasebeye çekmeli

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance benefits only its follower and error harms only its follower; no one bears another’s burden, and God does not punish until sending a messenger to convey guidance and error, after which acceptance or rejection is each person’s choice.
rows.anchor: Resûl gönderilince de hidâyet ve dalâlet tebliğ edilmiş bulunur. Fakat onu kabul edip etmemek herkesin kendi boynuna

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The principle also applies to societies: a community’s destruction comes from within, from the corrupt members whose wrongdoing is fastened to it.
rows.anchor: her cemiyetin yıkımı da kendi içinden, kendi boynuna geçirilen baykuşlarından nâşî olduğunu anlatmak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking the immediate life means working for the world and demanding one’s wages before death; God grants in this world only what He wills, to whom He wills, not necessarily the amount each person asks.
rows.anchor: dünya için çalışır, amelinin ecrini ölmeden bu hayât-ı dünyada almak isterse

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The value of a deed is determined by the one who employs and accepts it, not by the worker’s request; nevertheless Hud 11:15 promises full payment for their works with no one shortchanged.
rows.anchor: çalışanın istediği ile değil, çalıştıranın kabulü ile ta‘ayyün eder.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Immediate worldly preference may look pleasant at first, but its outcome is Hell, where the person is disgraced and expelled.
rows.anchor: işte acûl olmanın önü hoş gibi görünürse de âkıbeti böyle vahimdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife-seeker must pursue it with fitting effort while believing; such people’s striving is appreciated.
rows.anchor: ona iman ederek lâyıkı vechile sa‘y de eylerse

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sustains both worldly and afterlife seekers from His limitless grace, not as payment for their deeds; His gift is not withheld, so afterlife seekers should not assume they will lack worldly provision.
rows.anchor: amellerinin mukābili olarak değil, Rabbine mahsus olan nâmütenâhî atıyyeden sırf bahşiş olarak imdad ederiz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People in both groups differ greatly in worldly gifts and rank, a difference that comes solely from God’s preference and will.
rows.anchor: Bu fark u tefâvütün esası mahza Allah teâlâ’nın bir tercih ve tafdîlidir. Ve ancak O’nun eser-i meşiyyetidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife is greater in degrees and in the extent of divine preference, so people should not rush and should prefer it in all aims to make their striving appreciated.
rows.anchor: ve her hâlde âhiret derecâtca da daha büyük, tafdilce de daha büyüktür.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Associating another god with God leaves a person blameworthy, abandoned, and without a helper; shirk is the greatest injustice, whose wrongdoer is ultimately condemned and forsaken.
rows.anchor: şirk çok büyük zulüm, en büyük haksızlıktır, zâlim ise her zaman mezmum ve âkıbet mahzuldür.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every effort needs power; the greatest power is truth and truth begins with monotheism, making faith the first condition for afterlife-worthy striving and explaining why the commands begin with tawhid.
rows.anchor: En büyük kuvvet ise haktır. Hakkın başı da tevhiddir.

none: verse text and page marker only

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading is that if there were other gods, each would seek a way to overpower the Lord of the Throne, since a god would have to prevail; this is the argument from mutual prevention, also expressed in 21:22.
rows.anchor: Birisi her biri o Mâlikü’l-mülk’e galebe etmek çaresini arardı, çünkü gālib olmadan ilâh olamazdı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reading is that alleged gods would need to seek access to God and derive power from Him, recognizing that a polity needs a chief; this would concede His sole divinity.
rows.anchor: her biri O’nun Zât-ı ehadiyetinden kuvvet ve kudret iktisab etmeksizin bir şey yapamayacaklarını
